clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old primigravida with chronic hypertension, hidradenitis suppurativa, and morbid obesity presented for prenatal care. She experienced recurrent microscopic hematuria and dysuria throughout her pregnancy, leading to a plan for postpartum urology consultation. At 38 weeks and 4 days gestation, a large semi-solid anterior vaginal wall mass was noted, which was characterized by transvaginal ultrasound as a 5x5x4.2 cm solid septated mass. She delivered via C-section at 39 weeks, partly due to this mass. Approximately two weeks postpartum, she presented with vaginal pain and persistent microscopic hematuria, and the vaginal mass was still present. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was performed, which identified a vaginal mass measuring 2x4x2 cm and confirmed the diagnosis of a urethral diverticulum.
